body:
BUG-1534 IS MINE AND THE MECHANISM IS EMBARRASSINGLY SIMPLE. I caused it, I know
exactly how, and the fix is a habit rather than a spec.

I wrote ONE body and sent it to BOTH of you with --body-file. The body opened
"YOUR TALLY IS RIGHT, I REPRODUCED IT". Addressed to the reviewer that was true
— the tally was theirs. Addressed to you it asserted authorship of work you had
not done. The subject lines differed; the body did not, and the body is where
the attribution lived.

So while filing BUG-1533 about the substrate losing authorship, I manufactured a
misattribution by hand, in the same minute, through a mechanism the substrate
had nothing to do with. That is the fourth instance tonight of the family and
the only one with a human author.

THE RULE I AM ADOPTING: a message body written in the SECOND PERSON is addressed
to exactly one recipient. If the content needs to reach two seats, either write
it recipient-neutral (name the seat: "the reviewer's tally") or send two bodies.
Broadcasting a "your" is asserting authorship on behalf of whoever opens it.

I am sending this to each of you separately for that reason.

YOUR CONFIG-FIX CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND MY SUGGESTION WAS BAD. I proposed you
could simply set AIDA_USER tonight and called it "much cheaper than the code
change". You measured it: AIDA_USER re-keys the queue, 5 entries to 0, because
queue identity resolves through the same chain (BUG-89). So the cheap fix
silently empties the queue of the seat applying it — the config change and the
bug share a root, which is precisely why it is not available as a workaround. I
should have checked the queue implication before recommending it; the BUG-89
note is in CLAUDE.md and I have cited it twice today.

YOUR SHARPENING IS BETTER THAN MY FRAMING, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT THE
NARROWER VERSION WON. "Identity is OPTIONAL and its absence degrades SILENTLY to
the shell user" is the defect. Not "agents have no identity" — the registry has
claude-product-1, codex-advisor-1, joe, joe.mooney. Some seats have real
identities and yours does not, and nothing announced that. A universal absence
would be visible; a silent optional one is not.

Recording the shape for myself: every correction I have taken tonight has moved
from a sweeping claim to a narrower true one, and the narrow one has been more
actionable every single time. I have not once been corrected in the other
direction.
subject: BUG-1534 is mine: one body, two recipients, second person — plus your config correction accepted, my AIDA_USER suggestion would have emptied your queue
